title: Admin shortflow wizard and decision-tree caching
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: on-call engineers repeatedly run small, time-sensitive remediation flows that are ad-hoc, error-prone, and not instrumented. We need a lightweight 'shortflow' UX that converts curated runbook fragments into a guided, idempotent wizard with decision-tree caching so repeated remediation attempts are fast and safe. Goals: 1) reduce mean time to repair (MTTR) for common incidents by 30% for first-line responders, 2) ensure every shortflow emits structured telemetry (steps attempted, params, outcomes) and ties back to runbook provenance, 3) make flows idempotent and safe to re-run without manual state reconciliation, 4) expose a small on-call CLI and console surface for quick execution and audit.
acceptance_criteria: Shortflow authoring UI or manifest format documented and tested
Decision-tree caching implemented: prefix/KV cache with TTL and strong namespacing per-incident
All shortflows produce structured telemetry events consumed by ops-telemetry pipeline
Idempotency primitives (dry-run, transactional-apply, compensating-ops) available for each step
E2E smoke test that replays a shortflow against staging and verifies no side effects after repeat runs
RBAC gating and KMS-protected secrets access validated in Private deployments
Canary rollout to 20% of on-call teams with rollback plan and postmortem checklist
tasks: Design shortflow manifest schema (yaml) and CLI interface
Implement decision-tree cache layer in admin-runtime with namespaced keys
Add telemetry hooks: step_started, step_succeeded, step_failed, retry_count, final_outcome
Create idempotency helpers: deterministic-run-id, operation-safe-check, compensator registration
Integrate with runbook registry to surface provenance links in telemetry and audit logs
Write e2e smoke harness and chaos test for repeated execution
Submit PR and RFC for security review (KMS/privileged ops)
decisions: Use a manifest-first approach (yaml) instead of a full GUI authoring tool to accelerate adoption
Cache strategy: KV cache with 10m default TTL, per-incident namespace and step-level keys; allow overrides in manifest
Idempotency model: prefer safe-check+apply+compensator pattern over full transactional orchestration to keep runtime lightweight
Telemetry format: JSON lines with stable schema v1.0 (namespace, run_id, step, status, elapsed_ms, tags)
Security: secrets accessed via ephemeral KMS tokens; shortflow execution requires 'shortflow.execute' permission scoped to team
